chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman gave birth from adultery (zina). Should I take her as a wet-nurse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take her as a wet-nurse, nor her daughter.'

key_terms.تَسْتَرْضِعْهَا: Take her as a wet-nurse (imperative form)
key_terms.ظِئْرًا: Wet-nurse (a woman who breastfeeds a child other than her own)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take a woman who gave birth from zina as a wet-nurse?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a woman who gave birth from *zina* (illicit sexual relations) and her daughter are not to be taken as wet-nurses (*radhi'*). This establishes a specific legal status for them, often interpreted by Shia jurists as a form of ritual or legal impurity (*najis* or *ghayr maqbul*) affecting their milk, thereby preventing the formation of foster kinship (*muharramat*) through their nursing. The extension to the daughter highlights the generational transmission of this specific legal condition within the context of *rad al-sadr* (wet-nursing) laws.
